title: What is left over?
goal: I can divide with a remainder. I can decide what the remainder means in a story. I can find a mystery number.

learn.intro: When we share or make groups, some may be left over. The leftover is the remainder. It is always smaller than the number we divide by.

example.problem: Ali has 38 stickers. Each bag takes 5 stickers. How many bags can he fill? How many stickers are left over?
steps: Find the greatest fact that is not more than 38. 5 × 7 = 35.
Subtract to find what is left: 38 - 35 = 3.
example.answer: 7 full bags, with 3 stickers left over.

howto.title: How to divide with a remainder
steps: Find the greatest table fact that fits in the number.
Subtract it to find the remainder.
A leftover person still needs a seat: use 1 more group.

try.text: A baker packs 43 buns into boxes of 6. She fills {b} boxes and has {b} buns left over.

items.text: The dots are put into groups of 4.
items.explanation: Count the solid boxes: 4 groups of 4 dots make 16 dots. The dashed box has the 3 dots left over. So 19 ÷ 4 = 4 remainder 3.

items.text: Divide.
Divide. Then decide what the leftover means.

parts.label: a
parts.text: 26 people go in cars of 5. They need {b} cars.

parts.label: b
parts.text: 37 cm of ribbon, cut in 6 cm pieces, gives {b} whole pieces.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Ravi has $30. A toy costs $4. He buys {b} toys.

items.explanation: (a) 26 ÷ 5 = 5 remainder 1. The 1 person left over still needs a car, so 6 cars. (b) 37 ÷ 6 = 6 remainder 1: 6 whole pieces. (c) 30 ÷ 4 = 7 remainder 2: 7 toys. (d) The remainder is the money left: $2.

items.text: Kumar says 59 ÷ 7 = 7 remainder 10.
items.explanation: A remainder must be smaller than the number we divide by. 10 is greater than 7, so another group of 7 fits. 7 × 8 = 56 and 59 - 56 = 3. So 59 ÷ 7 = 8 remainder 3.

items.text: Ali stacks coins in piles of 5. He makes 9 full piles and has 4 coins left over.

parts.label: b
parts.text: He stacks all the coins again in piles of 6. He makes {b} piles and has {b} coins left.

items.explanation: (a) 9 × 5 = 45, and 45 + 4 = 49. (b) 49 ÷ 6: 6 × 8 = 48 and 49 - 48 = 1. So 8 full piles and 1 coin left.

items.text: Think about remainders.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
List every remainder that is possible when a number is divided by 5.
{ll}

parts.label: b
parts.text: A number between 50 and 60 is divided by 7. The remainder is as great as it can be. The number is {b}.

items.explanation: (a) A remainder is always smaller than 5, so it can be 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4. (b) The greatest remainder for 7 is 6. The numbers with remainder 6 are 6, 13, 20, ... 48, 55, 62. Only 55 is between 50 and 60.

items.text: Look for a pattern. Write the remainder when each number is divided by 4.

parts.label: b
parts.text: When 30 is divided by 4 the remainder is {b}.

parts.label: c
parts.text: When 100 is divided by 4 the remainder is {b}.

items.explanation: The remainders go 0, 1, 2, 3 and then start again. (b) 30 = 28 + 2, and 28 is in the 4 times table, so the remainder is 2. (c) 100 = 4 × 25, so the remainder is 0.

items.text: Find a number between 30 and 40. Dividing it by 6 gives remainder 1. Dividing it by 4 gives remainder 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The numbers that leave remainder 1 when divided by 6 are {b} and {b}.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The number I am looking for is {b}.

items.explanation: Between 30 and 40: 6 × 5 = 30 and 6 × 6 = 36, so the numbers are 31 and 37. Test with 4: 31 ÷ 4 = 7 remainder 3 (right). 37 ÷ 4 = 9 remainder 1 (not right). The number is 31.

items.text: 52 children go on a trip. Each bus has 9 seats.

parts.label: c
parts.text: {b} seats on the last bus are empty.

items.explanation: 52 ÷ 9 = 5 remainder 7. 5 full buses are not enough, because 7 children are left. So they need 6 buses. The last bus has 7 children, and 9 - 7 = 2 seats are empty.

items.text: The letters A, B, C and D repeat in this order.
items.explanation: The pattern repeats every 4 letters. 30 ÷ 4 = 7 remainder 2, so the 30th letter is the 2nd of the pattern: B. 32 ÷ 4 = 8 with none left, so the 32nd is the last: D.

items.text: Mei has 8 bags with 9 beads in each bag, and 5 loose beads. She shares all the beads equally among 9 friends.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Each friend gets {b} beads and {b} beads are left over.

items.explanation: (a) 8 × 9 = 72, and 72 + 5 = 77. (b) 77 ÷ 9: 9 × 8 = 72 and 77 - 72 = 5. Each friend gets 8 beads and 5 beads are left over.

items.text:
Circle each number that has remainder 3 when you divide it by 5.
{circ:18|23|33|41|48}
items.explanation: A number leaves remainder 3 when it is 3 more than a number in the 5 times table. 18 = 15 + 3, 23 = 20 + 3, 33 = 30 + 3, 48 = 45 + 3. 41 = 40 + 1 leaves remainder 1.

items.text: Divide 47 by each of 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8. Which number gives the greatest remainder?   {circ:4|5|6|7|8}
items.explanation: 47 ÷ 4 = 11 remainder 3. 47 ÷ 5 = 9 remainder 2. 47 ÷ 6 = 7 remainder 5. 47 ÷ 7 = 6 remainder 5. 47 ÷ 8 = 5 remainder 7. The greatest remainder is 7, from 8.

items.text: Today is Tuesday.

parts.label: a
parts.text: 45 days from today it will be   {circ:Mon|Tue|Wed|Thu|Fri|Sat|Sun}

items.explanation: (a) 45 ÷ 7 = 6 remainder 3. After 6 weeks it is Tuesday again. Then 3 more days: Wednesday, Thursday, Friday. (b) 20 ÷ 7 = 2 remainder 6. Go back 2 weeks to Tuesday, then back 6 more days: Wednesday.
items.hint: A week has 7 days. Divide by 7 and use the remainder.

items.text: Find the 2-digit number. Dividing it by 5 gives remainder 2. Dividing it by 3 gives remainder 1. Dividing it by 4 gives remainder 3. {b}
items.explanation: Numbers with remainder 2 when divided by 5 end in 2 or 7. 67 = 66 + 1 (66 is in the 3 times table) and 67 = 64 + 3 (64 is in the 4 times table). No other works.
items.hint: Begin with the clue that gives the fewest numbers to list.

items.text: Aisha shares crayons among her cousins. If each cousin gets 3 crayons, 11 crayons are not used. If each cousin gets 5 crayons, she needs 7 more. How many cousins are there? How many crayons does she have?
items.explanation: Giving each cousin 2 more crayons uses the 11 crayons that were not used and needs 7 more: 11 + 7 = 18 crayons. So 18 ÷ 2 = 9 cousins. The crayons: 9 × 3 + 11 = 38.
items.hint: Compare the 2 plans: each cousin gets 2 more crayons.

items.beyond: Remainders when you add and double
items.text: A number leaves remainder 3 when divided by 7.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Add 5 to it. The new remainder is {b}.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Double it. The new remainder is {b}.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Another number leaves 5 when divided by 8. Doubled, it leaves {b}.

items.explanation: (a) 3 + 5 = 8, and 8 ÷ 7 leaves 1. (b) 3 + 3 = 6, smaller than 7. (c) 5 + 5 = 10, and 10 ÷ 8 leaves 2. Test: 10 + 5 = 15 leaves 1; 20 leaves 6; 26 ÷ 8 leaves 2.
items.hint: Try a number like 10 (remainder 3 when divided by 7). Test it.

items.text: Ali has between 20 and 100 marbles. Counting in 3s leaves 1 over. Counting in 4s leaves 2 over. Counting in 5s leaves 3 over. How many marbles does he have? {b}
items.explanation: Each clue is 2 short of a full group: 1 left in 3s, 2 left in 4s and 3 left in 5s. So the number is 2 less than a number in the 3, 4 and 5 times tables. The first one is 60, so the number is 58.
items.hint: Compare each clue with a full group.

items.text: Make up your own number riddle: a range and 2 remainder clues. Only ONE number may fit. Swap with a grown-up.

answer.text: Answers vary. Example: I am between 10 and 25. When I am divided by 4 the remainder is 1. When I am divided by 3 the remainder is 2. The only number is 17.

items.explanation: Test each with the second clue. In the example, the numbers with remainder 1 when divided by 4 are 13, 17 and 21. Only 17 leaves remainder 2 when divided by 3.
items.hint: Pick your number first. Then find its remainders.

items.text: Ben sells eggs in boxes of 3 and boxes of 5. An order must be whole boxes.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Can he fill an order for 11 eggs?   {circ:Yes|No}

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Orders from 1 to 15 he CANNOT fill:
{ll}

items.hint: List the orders he can fill. Which numbers are missing?

items.text: Divide. 52 ÷ 8 = {b} remainder {b}
A bus holds 9 people. How many buses are needed for 40 people? {b}
items.explanation: 40 ÷ 9 = 4 remainder 4. The 4 people left over need another bus: 5 buses.

items.text: Mei packs 25 muffins into boxes of 6. How many muffins are left over? {b}
items.explanation: 6 × 4 = 24 and 25 - 24 = 1. One muffin is left over.

items.text: Find a number between 20 and 30. It leaves remainder 2 when divided by 3 and remainder 4 when divided by 5. {b}
items.explanation: The numbers from 20 to 30 that leave remainder 2 when divided by 3 are 20, 23, 26 and 29. Of these, only 29 leaves remainder 4 when divided by 5 (25 + 4).
